about: Hand-curated registry of the property keys the Forge bridge emits on tokens, action options and records. Each component of a token is encoded as (key embedding, value repr); the key embedding is the frozen text embedding of `description`. Counter keys are expanded from counter_keys.json (generated from Forge by scripts/gen_counter_keys.py). tests/test_keys.py fails when the bridge emits a key that is not here. Layout (schema 9): `identity` and `ref` keys sit at the top level of a token next to `type`, `zone` and `edges`; every other key (number/flag/string/string_list) is nested under the token's `components` object, which is omitted when empty, and flags appear only when true. magicnet.bridge.Schema.isTopLevel implements this split and tests/test_schema.py checks it against this file. Action options and the record envelope are not tokens and stay flat. Schema 13: history tokens carry no refs; participants are edges (see magicnet.schema.RELATIONS) and closed-vocabulary components are `categorical` with a `vocab` named in magicnet.schema.VOCABS.

value_kinds.string: short string; embed the value with the catalog's text embedder (POST /strings/embed)
value_kinds.string_list: list of short strings; embed each and pool
value_kinds.categorical: value from a closed vocabulary named by the key's `vocab`; look up a learned embedding per vocabulary (shared across keys with the same vocab)
value_kinds.ref: names or points at another object/player; top-level (not under components); should become an edge
value_kinds.identity: join key / token identity, not a component; top-level; never encoded as (key, value)

keys.notes: Selects the encoder (schema.ENCODER_MAPPING); not a component.
Values are magicnet.schema.ZONES (index with schema.zone_index). Stays at the token top level: it is also structural (sides, masking, segment embedding).
Resolved to relation-aware attention bias, not a component.
Join key for edges; stripped by dump.strip_ids. On history tokens (schema 13): e<N>, the event's index in this viewer's history, which cause and affected_by edges point at.

Embedded even when oracle_id is present: names are part of the rules grammar ("cards named X", "with X in its name"). Absent on an object the viewer cannot see (schema 12; per the rules an unseen or face-down card has no name), including the hidden-sideboard/library count aggregates; such tokens carry no oracle_id either. Test with magicnet.dump.is_hidden. Stays at the token top level for redaction checks. Phantoms (schema 13) carry the last-known name; an ability phantom carries its source's name.
Join to the card catalog.
On history tokens: the turn the event happened in (0 = pregame).

Schema 14, phantoms only: true for a token that left the battlefield or a copy/ability that left the stack; absent on an identity phantom (a card the viewer lost track of, which still exists somewhere it cannot tell: "a copy of X").

keys.description: tracking handles assigned to this token
keys.notes: Schema 13: the h<N> handles history edges point at that this token currently stands for (the object itself, the aggregate of the hidden zone it is in, the owner's untracked token, or a phantom). Each referenced handle is on exactly one token per state. Resolved by dump.resolve_edges; stripped by dump.strip_ids.
Schema 13; values magicnet.schema.HISTORY_VERBS. Replaces `event`.

keys.description: which atomic game action this event was part of, counted from the start of the game
keys.notes: Schema 13: one step per resolution, cast/activation (with its costs), combat-damage batch, state-based-action check or turn-based action; events of one simultaneous batch share it. Counted per viewer over the events that viewer sees.

keys.description: order of this event within its step
keys.notes: Schema 13; 0-based.

Schema 13, on every history token: pointer (a consequence of the events its cause edges point at), turn_based, state_based (may also carry a cause edge to the lethal damage), combat, pregame, player_action or unknown.
Schema 13 move_zone: put, mill, exile, sacrifice, destroy, bounce, search, return or other.

keys.description: why the spell or ability did not resolve
keys.notes: Schema 13 does_not_resolve: countered (cause edge: the counterspell's resolve), fizzled (all targets illegal), removed (left the stack otherwise).

Schema 13 designation_change: monarch, initiative, city's blessing, speed, day, night.
Schema 13 special_action: turn_face_up, foretell, plot, unlock, or the Forge ability api lowercased (e.g. changezone for a companion).

patterns.notes: Expanded concretely from counter_keys.json; an unseen counter still gets "<name> counters".
AttemptEnd: values announced while casting (X, multikicker count, ...).

role_java_exprs_about: Dynamic key expressions allowed without a pattern. Schema 13: m.getKey() is GameHistory.append copying a history record's modifier map onto the token; those keys are scanned where HistoryHub writes them (r.mods.put). History participants are edges (magicnet.schema.RELATIONS), not role-named keys.
record_fields_about: Serializer's decision-record envelope. Not token components, except kind/turn/phase which are registered keys (turn and phase duplicate the global token).
